channel.title: Happy News Company
channel.description: Real, sourced good news and good-news press releases

item.title: Namibia's Lion Rangers Pair Smartphones With Traditional Tracking Skills to Protect Desert Lions
item.description: Local rangers across 11 conservancies have eliminated illegal lion killings in six of them, though drought-driven prey loss keeps conflict a challenge.

item.title: Sheffield Scientist Recreates the Roman Glass That Changes Color Under Light
item.description: After 1,600 years, a University of Sheffield team has reproduced the dichroic effect of the famed Lycurgus Cup using only ingredients the Romans had.

item.title: Googly-Eyed Buoys and Bird-of-Prey Kites Cut Seabird Bycatch in Cornish Fishing Nets
item.description: A field trial with 10 Cornish fishers found kites lowered the odds of catching guillemots and razorbills by 71%, and eye-shaped buoys by 59%.

item.title: Netherlands Pledges Up to $500 Million to Protect Tropical Forests
item.description: The Dutch government says it will contribute to the Tropical Forest Forever Facility over ten years, a fund designed to pay countries for keeping forests standing.

item.title: London's Oxford Street Goes Car-Free, Giving Pedestrians Nearly a Kilometre of Europe's Busiest Shopping Street
item.description: Traffic is out and trees, seating and two new public squares are on the way, as the city bets on people on foot.

item.title: A Small Scottish Island's Historical Society Uncovers a Major Early Medieval Monastery
item.description: Community-funded excavations on Lismore found burials, craft workshops and evidence of gold and silver working at the site of a sixth-century monastery.

item.title: Felicia and Ben Horowitz Commit $150 Million to Nevada's First Standalone Children's Hospital
item.description: Intermountain Health says the gift is one of the largest ever made to a U.S. children's hospital and will fund specialists, programs and research in Las Vegas.

item.title: More Than $42 Million in Medical Debt Erased for Nearly 27,000 Kansans
item.description: A civic group bought the debt through the nonprofit Undue Medical Debt, and recipients are getting letters saying their old bills are paid.

item.title: New Study Suggests Van Gogh's "Starry Night" Shows a Real Sky Over Saint-Rémy in July 1889
item.description: Researchers say the painting's crescent moon, Venus and star cluster match the pre-dawn view of 22 July 1889.

item.title: Three Michigan Tribes Are Working to Bring Back a Fish Missing for Nearly a Century
item.description: Young Arctic grayling and hundreds of thousands of eggs have been released, though success will take years to judge.

item.title: Orphaned Walrus Calf Found Between Two Carcasses in Alaska Gets a New Home in Florida
item.description: A student researcher spotted the calf's stomach move; weeks later, five-month-old Annautaq is settling in at SeaWorld Orlando.

item.title: [Press Release] Squamish Sauna Hat Shop Is Giving Away Free Wool Sauna Hats This Christmas
item.description: Sauna Hats Canada will send a grey wool bucket sauna hat to anyone in Canada who joins its list. Customers pay only the shipping.

item.title: [Press Release] Squamish Photographer Opens Library of Sea to Sky Stock Photos, Licensed Directly With No Subscription
item.description: Jeremy Allen of The Full Time Hobby has put hundreds of photos of Squamish, Whistler and British Columbia online for businesses to license direct from the photographer.

item.title: FDA Approves Hibsago, the First Antisense Treatment for Chronic Hepatitis B
item.description: Used alongside existing antivirals, the injection let nearly one in five trial participants keep the virus under control after stopping all hepatitis B medicine.

item.title: Samoa's Nu'utele Island Bounces Back a Year After Invasive Rats and Pigs Were Removed
item.description: Native seedlings carpet the forest floor, ground doves are nesting, and turtles have returned, Island Conservation reports.

item.title: Chiricahua's Rock Spires Become America's 64th National Park
item.description: The Arizona site, a national monument since 1924, is the first new national park in six years.

item.title: Basic Income Pilot With Indigenous Peruvian Communities Cuts Food Insecurity From 73% to 26%
item.description: Two years of unconditional cash, about £2 a day, also coincided with widespread reforestation and spring-restoration work.

item.title: Allegheny County Passes Nation's First Countywide Paid Parental Leave, Led by Nurses
item.description: A campaign started by Pittsburgh hospital nurses ended with an 11-4 council vote for 12 weeks of paid leave.

item.title: A New UK Scheme Is Certifying Solar Farms That Help Wildlife
item.description: Wild Power's scorecard rewards developers for habitat corridors and hedgerows, and an Essex site is the second to earn certification.

item.title: FDA Approves Immunotherapy That May Let Some Rectal Cancer Patients Skip Chemo, Radiation and Surgery
item.description: Jemperli is cleared for adults with a rare tumor subtype, and in a trial almost three-quarters of patients did not need those treatments.

item.title: ETH Zurich Chemists Find a Gentler Way to Recycle Acrylic Glass Into Like-New Plastic
item.description: A single inexpensive reagent lets acrylic break down at just over 200°C, recovering up to 98% of its building blocks.

item.title: Japan Launches MMX, a Mission to Bring Home the First Samples From a Martian Moon
item.description: JAXA's spacecraft is on its way to Phobos, with NASA, ESA, France and Germany contributing and samples due back on Earth by 2031.

item.title: Mozambique Protects Mount Mabu's "Butterfly Forest" as a Community-Run Conservation Area
item.description: A new decree hands stewardship of 9,341 hectares of rare mid-altitude rainforest to the local communities who kept it standing.

item.title: Amsterdam Zoo Gives a Southern Ground Hornbill a 3D-Printed Beak
item.description: Vets at ARTIS and Utrecht University replaced both the upper and lower beak, and the bird was using them within hours.

item.title: New York City Will Expand Free 2-K to 12,000 Two-Year-Olds Across 22 Districts
item.description: Next fall's seats are a sixfold jump from this year's 2,000, including every district in the Bronx and Staten Island.

item.title: [Press Release] Squamish Web Designer Launches Free Website Program for Small Businesses Across Canada
item.description: FreeSite Company builds custom, hand-coded websites for free. Owners see the finished site before paying anything, and keep it online for $9.99 a month only if they love it.

item.title: [Press Release] Squamish Canoe Rental Publishes Free Cold-Water Safety Guide as Paddlers Head Out for Fall
item.description: The guide explains the 1-10-1 rule, what to wear and which Sea to Sky lakes are best when the water turns cold.

item.title: John Paulson Gives Hebrew University a Record $250 Million
item.description: The gift, announced at the university's board gala, will fund a new engineering faculty, biomedical research and trauma-recovery studies.

item.title: India Moves to Cut Prices of 137 Cancer Drugs by Up to 70%
item.description: A cap on distribution and retail margins takes effect on November 9, building on a 2019 scheme for 42 medicines.

item.title: Greenland's Parliament Votes Unanimously to Back a Deep-Sea Mining Ban
item.description: Lawmakers directed the government to write rules barring seabed mineral extraction until at least the end of 2029.

item.title: 24-Year Study Finds Some German Forest Soils Are Absorbing More Methane
item.description: Göttingen researchers saw methane uptake climb about 3% a year at 13 sites, challenging the idea that forest soils are steadily losing this ability.

item.title: Milwaukee's Havenwoods State Forest Opens a Braille Trail
item.description: The third-of-a-mile loop combines tactile signs, audio and loaner white canes so blind and low-vision visitors can explore the forest.

item.title: Brazil's Amazon Deforestation Falls to the Lowest Level on Record
item.description: Satellite data show clearing down about 42% in a year, the lowest since official monitoring began in 1988.

item.title: American Prairie's Free-Roaming Bison Herd Passes 1,000 for the First Time
item.description: The Montana conservation nonprofit counted 1,016 bison after this year's calves, and a federal judge has let the herd stay on key grazing land while a legal fight continues.

item.title: Five New Rain Frogs Described From Peru's Amazon Lowlands and Andean Slopes
item.description: Herpetologists led by Pablo Venegas formally named the species in Zootaxa, from sites ranging from 183 to 1,778 metres in elevation.

item.title: A Bangladeshi Rug Factory Designed Around Its Workers Wins the 2026 RIBA International Prize
item.description: Green Field Factory in Rangpur, home to about 5,000 mostly female workers, features courtyards, gardens, a rooftop daycare and an on-site medical practice.

item.title: Illinois Has Erased $1.4 Billion in Medical Debt for About 694,000 Residents
item.description: The state's two-year-old program needs no application, and Cook County says it will keep funding its own effort.

item.title: Brazil's Senate Votes 75–1 to End the Six-Day Workweek
item.description: A constitutional amendment will cut the standard week from 44 to 40 hours and guarantee two paid rest days, without lowering pay.

item.title: Bleached Coral Recovered After Touching a Healthy Clone, Stanford Lab Study Finds
item.description: Early lab research shows bleached fragments regained their color in about seven weeks, though the method is not yet a reef-scale fix.

item.title: Seabirds and Native Forests Could Help Low-Lying Atolls Keep Pace With Rising Seas
item.description: A Science Advances study of 28 atoll islands found reefs grew up to 2.5 times faster around rat-free, seabird-rich islands.
